newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica retailers optimistic despite Q4 sales drop.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica retailers optimistic despite Q4 sales drop.

text.p: Retail sales volumes grew 2.5 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996, down from 4.2 percent in the third quarter, the University of Stellenbosch's Bureau for Economic Research said on Wednesday.
But despite the fall in volumes, the level of retailer business confidence rose.
"At first sight, this would appear to be somewhat contradictory," BER said in a statement.
"However, the rise in the level of business confidence is on par with the bottoming out of expectations regarding business conditions and sales volumes.
"In each of the last three surveys, respondents did not expect a further deterioration in business conditions or larger declines in sales volumes."
The level of business confidence of wholesalers rose to 48 percent from 21 percent.
This was mainly due to continued buoyant sales of non-consumer goods, mainly machinery for agriculture, mining and industry, and a smaller than expected deterioration in business conditions, it said.
